title: リモートワークの是非
lines: A
I honestly don't think I could go back to working in an office five days a week.
B
I get that, but don't you miss bumping into people and having quick chats?
A
Sometimes, sure. But I'd rather have an extra two hours a day than spend them commuting.
B
Fair enough. Still, I've noticed new hires seem to learn a lot faster when they're around experienced staff.
A
That's a good point. Maybe a hybrid setup is the best of both worlds.

オフィスの方が集中できる
questions.explain: 通勤に2時間使うより在宅を好んでいます。

questions.q: B が指摘した出社の利点は？
choices: 新人が経験者の近くで速く学べる
questions.explain: new hires seem to learn a lot faster when they're around experienced staff

title: ニュース：交通政策
lines: A
The city council has approved a plan to make public buses free for residents under 18.
A
Officials say the scheme, which begins in April, is aimed at reducing traffic around schools.
A
It's expected to cost around 3 million dollars a year, funded partly by a new parking fee.
A
Critics argue the money would be better spent improving existing routes.
A
The council says it will review the results after twelve months.

choices: 全市民のバスを無料化
18歳未満の住民のバスを無料化
既存路線の改善に使うべき

title: 製品発表
lines: A
When we started designing this headset, we kept hearing the same complaint: it hurts after an hour.
A
So instead of adding more features, we focused almost entirely on comfort.
A
The new model is thirty percent lighter, and the battery lasts a full working day.
A
We've also made the ear cushions replaceable, so you won't have to throw the whole thing away.
A
It goes on sale next month, starting at 149 dollars.

questions.q: 開発で最も重視したことは？
questions.explain: we focused almost entirely on comfort

questions.q: 新モデルの特徴として正しいのは？

title: 講義：記憶と忘却
lines: A
In the 1880s, a German researcher named Hermann Ebbinghaus tested his own memory using lists of nonsense syllables.
A
He found that we forget most new information within the first day, and then the rate of forgetting slows down.
A
What's interesting is that each time he reviewed the material, it took longer to forget.
A
This is the basic idea behind spaced repetition, which many learning apps rely on today.
A
In other words, it's not how long you study, but when you review that really matters.

questions.q: エビングハウスの発見は？
choices: 新しい情報の多くは最初の1日で忘れ、その後忘れる速度は落ちる
復習しても忘れる速さは同じ
無意味な音節は覚えやすい
questions.explain: forget most new information within the first day, then the rate slows down

choices: 長時間勉強することが大事
いつ復習するかが大事
アプリは役に立たない
questions.explain: it's not how long you study, but when you review that really matters

title: 取引の交渉
lines: A
We're very interested, but the price is a bit higher than we'd budgeted for.
B
I understand. What kind of figure did you have in mind?
A
If you could bring it down by ten percent, we'd be ready to sign today.
B
Ten percent is difficult. But if you commit to a two-year contract, I could offer seven.
A
Let me run that by my manager, and I'll get back to you this afternoon.

questions.q: B が提示した条件は？
questions.explain: if you commit to a two-year contract, I could offer seven

choices: 上司に相談して午後に返事をする
questions.explain: Let me run that by my manager, and I'll get back to you this afternoon.

title: 就職面接
lines: A
Can you tell me about a time you had to deal with a difficult client?
B
Sure. In my last job, a client kept changing the requirements at the last minute.
B
Rather than arguing, I set up a short weekly call so we could agree on priorities early.
A
And how did that work out?
B
Pretty well, actually. We finished the project on time, and they've hired us twice since then.

choices: 直前に要件を変え続けた
questions.explain: kept changing the requirements at the last minute

choices: 毎週短い電話で優先順位を早めに合意した
questions.explain: a short weekly call so we could agree on priorities early

title: ラジオ：街の緑化
lines: A
Joining me today are two guests to talk about the city's plan to plant ten thousand trees.
B
Thanks for having me. Trees can lower street temperatures by several degrees in summer.
C
I agree they're important, but my concern is maintenance. Who's going to water them?
B
That's actually part of the plan. Local volunteers will adopt the trees on their street.
C
That sounds nice in theory, but volunteer programs often lose interest after a year or two.

questions.q: B が述べた木の効果は？
choices: 夏の路上の気温を数度下げる
questions.explain: lower street temperatures by several degrees in summer

choices: ボランティアの関心が続かず維持管理が難しい
questions.explain: maintenance と volunteer programs often lose interest を心配しています。

title: 起業ストーリー
lines: A
We launched our first app in a tiny shared office, and for six months, almost nobody downloaded it.
A
We were about to give up when we noticed that a small group of teachers were using it every single day.
A
So we interviewed them and realized they were using it for something we'd never intended.
A
We rebuilt the whole product around that one use case, and within a year, we had fifty thousand users.

choices: ほとんどダウンロードされなかった
想定外の使い方をしていた教師たちに注目した
questions.explain: 教師たちが意図しない用途で使っていたことに気づき、それに合わせて作り直しました。
